scenario.draft: Test the ability to retrieve a paginated, filtered, and sorted list of point wallet transaction histories as an admin. Include scenarios where filters are used for wallet, transaction_type, date range, and actor; verify that only authorized admin access is allowed. Successful tests should return appropriately filtered/paginated results. Failure scenarios include malformed filters and unauthorized access attempts, both of which must return appropriate error responses. Also test for empty result sets when queries do not match any records.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new customer point wallet to serve as the basis for searching and assigning point transactions.
Insert one or more transaction histories with known properties for search and pagination testing.

scenario.draft: Test fetching the details of a single point wallet transaction history record by its pointHistoryId as an admin. Begin by creating a point wallet and a corresponding transaction, then attempt a successful retrieval. Also, include negative scenarios such as attempting to access a non-existent transaction or using an invalid/deleted pointHistoryId. Unauthorized access by non-admin roles must result in error. All accesses should trigger audit logging.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a customer point wallet to which transactions will be added.
Create a transaction history record to be read by its ID in this scenario.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new point wallet transaction history as an admin, ensuring all required fields are validated and properly persisted. Success scenario involves providing valid wallet and transaction data, receiving the created transaction object, and verifying its audit attributes. Also test failure scenarios: 1) missing or invalid required fields (such as invalid wallet reference), 2) violation of business logic (e.g., recording a transaction against a non-existent wallet), and 3) ensuring audit logs capture creation. If attempting to create a duplicate transaction or out-of-bounds adjustment, an explicit error must be returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create the point wallet needed as a reference to attach a new history transaction.

scenario.draft: Test updating allowed fields for a specific point wallet transaction (pointHistoryId) as an admin. Start by creating a wallet and an associated transaction, then update mutable fields (such as remarks or admin logs). Attempt both valid updates and prohibited updates (such as trying to change immutable core transaction attributes). Unauthorized, invalid update or reference to a non-existing transaction should yield proper errors. All changes must be audit-logged.

dependencies.purpose: Create a point wallet to associate with the transaction history.
Create a point transaction record that can be updated in the test.

scenario.draft: Test the soft-delete operation for a point wallet transaction history by pointHistoryId as an admin. First, create a wallet and a transaction. Successfully deleting should set the deleted_at field, preserve the record for audit, and remove it from active queries. Attempting to delete an already deleted or non-existent history should result in an appropriate success or error response (idempotency or not found). Also ensure that all operations trigger audit logs for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create the customer point wallet needed for the transaction history.
Insert a valid transaction record that will be deleted during the test.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving detailed information for a specific product content (such as an image, video, or document) by its unique productContentId under the given productId as a seller. First, ensure a seller account exists and is authenticated. Next, create a product, then add content (e.g., image) to the product. Attempt to retrieve the content's detail as the owner seller, expecting full access to all fields defined in the response. Also include a scenario where a different seller or an unauthorized role attempts access, confirming proper error handling for forbidden access or not found errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller account to act as the product owner.
Seller creates a new product to which content will be attached.
Add a content entry to the product to set up productContentId.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can fetch the complete detail of a product content by providing valid productId and productContentId. First, create a product and add product content via an authenticated seller. Then, attempt to retrieve this content as an admin and verify that all content fields (including status, content_uri, content_type, etc.) are returned. Also, cover error handling for invalid IDs (product not found or content not found) and soft-deleted content (verify the correct error is returned).

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for authorization to fetch content details.
Register a seller for product/content creation, as only sellers can initially add products and content.
Seller creates a new product.
Add a content record to the product for test retrieval by admin.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new product content item (e.g., adding an image or video) for a specified product as a seller. Steps: Register a seller, create a product, then submit a valid product content creation payload (content_type, content_uri, ordering, status). Validate successful creation with all required fields. Test validation errors for missing required fields, invalid content_type, or malformed content_uri. Also test business rule violation such as attempting to add duplicate content with same ordering for the same product.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as a seller.
Create the owning product for content creation.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can create new product content for a specified product. First, set up an admin account and ensure a product exists. Attempt to create product content with valid fields as admin. Validate success and check that the record is associated correctly. Also, test error scenarios: creating content for a non-existent product (should fail with not found) and providing invalid/missing required fields (should yield validation errors).

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for admin-privileged content creation.
Register a seller to create the base product.
Create a product as seller (since only sellers can register products).

scenario.draft: Test updating an existing product content entity (such as correcting its content_type, updating its description, or changing its status) as the owning seller. First, create a seller and a product, then add a content entity to it. Next, issue a valid update as the owner seller and validate the changes. Additionally, cover negative scenarios where update is attempted with invalid data (violating schema or business rules), or by a different (non-owner) seller, confirming permission denial. Also test update on soft-deleted content (should result in not found or error).

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller for full content lifecycle tests.
Create a new product to act as parent for the content resource.
Create the content entity to obtain a productContentId for updating.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin user can access the complete details for a specific product bundle under any product, regardless of seller ownership. Set up a product and bundle as a seller, then authenticate as admin and attempt to retrieve the bundle's details by productId and productBundleId. Validate all schema fields and ensure the response includes even non-public admin metadata if expected. Missing or unauthorized access must return appropriate errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register (or authenticate) an admin user for privileged access.
Register a seller to create a product and bundle for testing purposes.
Create a product as the test seller, required for bundle association.
Create a product bundle under the created product so there is a bundle to fetch.

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can successfully create a product bundle for one of their own products. The scenario should include registering a seller, creating a product, and then issuing a request to create a bundle. Verify that bundle creation fails if required attributes are missing or if the seller attempts to create the bundle under a product they don't own. Validate returned fields upon creation and ensure audit metadata is recorded. Attempt to create a duplicate bundle and expect a validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate the seller for creating entities.
Set up a product to which a bundle will be added.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can create a product bundle on behalf of any product in the system. Set up a product as a seller, then authenticate as an admin and attempt to create a product bundle under the productId. Verify that admin permissions suffice, returned information matches expectations, and all required fields are enforced. Test creation failure when required fields are omitted or referential integrity fails (e.g., using invalid productId).

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin for privileged product and bundle management.
Register a seller to create a product which the admin can use for bundle testing.
Create a product as this seller for the admin to assign a bundle to.

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can update the details of an existing product bundle they own. The flow should create a seller, a product, a bundle, then update the bundle's name, description, status, or price using this endpoint. Validate that updates are applied and reflected in subsequent GET responses. If a seller attempts to update a bundle for a product they don't own, verify that an unauthorized error is returned. Invalid updates (such as missing required fields or failed validation) must also be tested and confirmed to fail with meaningful errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller for product/bundle management.
Create a product for bundle testing.
Create an initial product bundle before attempting update.

scenario.draft: Verify that an administrator can successfully update a product tag's attributes (such as the tag string or metadata) for a valid product and tag ID. First, ensure a product and at least one product tag exists by creating them if necessary. Then, perform a valid update operation, and confirm that the tag's data is modified accordingly in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product to which the tag will be attached.
Add an initial tag to the product to set up for tag update.

scenario.draft: Test updating a tag for a non-existent product or productTagId. Attempt an update with invalid IDs and confirm that the operation fails with a not found error indicating the tag or product is missing.

Validate that an unauthorized user (non-admin or lacking appropriate permissions) cannot update a product tag. Attempt to perform a tag update without admin credentials, expecting a permission denied error with an appropriate message.

Verify that a seller is able to successfully delete (remove or soft-delete) a specific tag from their own product. The test must first create a seller account, a product owned by that seller, and then a tag on that product. After setup, the seller should delete the tag and verify that the tag is removed (e.g., via list/search endpoint or by absence on get).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller account who will own the product.
Create a product under the seller's ownership.
Add a tag to the seller's product for deletion test.

scenario.draft: Try to delete a tag from a product as a seller using non-existent productId or productTagId, and confirm the error message or code reflects resource not found. No deletion should occur in this scenario.

Attempt to delete a tag from another seller's product and assert that the operation fails with an appropriate permission denied or forbidden error. This ensures that sellers can only manage tags on their own products.

dependencies.purpose: Register a second seller who will attempt the unauthorized deletion.
A product owned by the first seller with a tag, which the second seller will try to delete.

scenario.draft: Ensure that an admin can delete (remove or soft-delete) a specific tag from any product. After setting up a product and attaching a tag, perform the delete as an admin and verify via search or get that the tag is no longer present or is properly soft-deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product as setup target for tagging and deletion.
Attach a tag to the product as a setup step.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a tag for an invalid productId or productTagId by admin and verify that it returns an error signifying that the resource does not exist. No side effects should occur.
Attempt to perform a tag delete as a non-admin account. The test should ensure that only authorized admin users can perform this action and that unauthorized attempts are rejected with a clear error.

As a seller, retrieve a paginated and filtered list of search keywords assigned to one of their products. Set up by creating a seller, a product, and several search keywords for it. Execute the search (with and without filters such as keyword string, pagination, etc.) and verify the response contains the expected search keyword entries and metadata.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account to use throughout this workflow.
Create a product for the seller.
Add several keywords to the product to enable meaningful search.

scenario.draft: Search for keywords on a seller product that has no keywords attached and verify the result is an empty set (validating pagination and edge case handling). This confirms the search endpoint gracefully handles products with no keywords.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller for product setup.
Create a product with no attached search keywords yet.

scenario.draft: Attempt to search keywords on a product not owned by the seller and assert that the operation fails with a permission denied or forbidden error. This verifies that sellers are restricted to their own products' data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a second seller who will attempt to search another seller's product.
Create a product owned by a different seller.

scenario.draft: As an administrator, perform a paginated and filtered search of search keywords for a specific product. Prepare by creating a product with multiple keywords and then perform the keyword search with various filters (e.g., by keyword string, status, or use pagination). Validate that all assigned keywords are retrievable and filters work as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product that will have search keywords attached.
Attach multiple keywords to the product to set up for keyword search.

scenario.draft: Attempt to search for keywords for a non-existent product (invalid productId) as admin. Verify the operation fails gracefully, returning an appropriate error that the product is not found.
Attempt to search search keywords as a non-admin or unauthorized user. Confirm the system forbids access and presents a permission denied error.

Test successful soft deletion of a customer profile by an admin. First, an admin user registers, logs in, and creates a customer account (with separate profile). The admin then soft deletes the customer's profile via this endpoint and verifies that the profile is hidden from business processes but retained for audit (via customer_histories). Attempts to fetch this profile after deletion must fail or indicate non-existence. Confirm the customer cannot log in or perform business actions after soft deletion. Audit the action in customer_histories to validate compliance logging.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to perform administrative actions.
Authenticate as admin to acquire authorization for privileged operations.
Register a new customer account to be soft-deleted.

scenario.draft: Test soft delete failure when attempting to delete a customer profile that is already soft-deleted. First, an admin creates and then soft deletes a customer profile. The admin then attempts to delete the same customer profile again. The system must return an appropriate error response indicating that the customer does not exist or is already deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for the test.
Authenticate as admin.
Register a new customer to delete.
Delete the customer before retrying deletion to simulate double-deletion.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where a customer successfully soft deletes their own profile. First, a customer registers and logs in. The customer then sends a request to delete their own profile. Afterwards, verify the account cannot be used to log in and is absent from listings, but the audit log in customer_histories remains intact for compliance. Ensure all related addresses and resources remain unaffected unless otherwise specified.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer for the account self-deletion scenario.
Authenticate the customer prior to self-initiated deletion.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when a customer attempts to soft-delete their profile after it has already been deleted. Register and log in as a customer, delete the profile, and attempt to delete it again. The response must indicate the customer is already deleted or not found, preventing redundant operations.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer.
Authenticate as the customer.
Delete the customer profile prior to attempting double deletion.

scenario.draft: Test admin's ability to fetch a paginated and filtered list of addresses for a specific customer. First, an admin account is created and logged in, as well as a customer with multiple addresses linked. The admin uses this endpoint with various filters (e.g., city, state, is_primary) and pagination parameters to list and search the customer's addresses. Confirm only addresses meeting filter criteria are returned, and pagination works as expected. Verify that addresses for non-existent customerId yield the proper error.

dependencies.purpose: Establish admin privileges for the operation.
Authenticate the admin for subsequent actions.
Register a new customer to create addresses for.
Create several addresses for the test customer before listing and filtering.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where a logged-in customer retrieves their own active addresses using diverse filters and pagination. First, register and log in as a customer and create multiple addresses. Fetch paginated addresses, applying filters such as alias, is_primary, or city. Confirm only the customer's addresses are returned and privacy is enforced (no access to other customers' addresses). Also, test edge case of querying with an invalid or unauthorized customerId to ensure privacy is not breached and errors are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a customer account for the self-address listing scenario.
Obtain a customer session/auth token.
Create addresses for the customer before listing.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of an admin to successfully fetch a specific customer address using customerId and addressId. First, an admin registers and logs in, creates a customer, then adds an address for that customer. The admin fetches the newly created address by ID and verifies all fields are returned. Next, test that fetching a non-existent or unauthorized address (wrong customerId/addressId pair) returns a proper error. Also confirm that admins cannot access addresses of already-deleted customers.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin to authorize the retrieval.
Log in as admin for access rights.
Register a new customer for the test.
Create an address for the customer before fetching it.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a product option's details by an admin. First, create a product as an admin, then add a product option to this product, and finally as an admin user, request the details for the specific option using its productId and productOptionId. Confirm that the response includes all expected product option fields and observes data masking/visibility as per admin role.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new product as an admin to provide a valid productId.
Add a product option to the product to obtain a valid productOptionId.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval failure when requesting a nonexistent product option. As an admin, attempt to retrieve a product option using a productId and productOptionId pair that do not exist or are not linked. Expect a not found error with the appropriate status code and message.

Test access control by attempting to fetch a product option's details as a non-admin or non-authorized user. This should result in a permission denied error, demonstrating enforcement of role-based access control. No product creation required, as the focus is unauthorized access.

Test successful creation of a new product option by a seller for their own product. Register a seller, log in, create a product as the seller, then attempt to create a product option under this product. Validate that all required fields and business logic constraints are enforced, and that the result returns expected data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account to obtain valid credentials.
Obtain seller JWT for authenticated actions.
Create a product as the seller, providing a valid productId.

scenario.draft: Test failure when attempting to create a product option with a duplicate SKU under the same product as a seller. Ensure the first product option is created successfully, then create a second with the same SKU and expect a validation error for duplicate constraint.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account for authentication.
Get JWT for seller session.
Create a seller's product for option association.
Create the first product option and get the SKU for duplication.

scenario.draft: Test that invalid input (missing required fields or invalid field formats) is properly rejected when a seller attempts to create a product option. Attempt creation with missing or malformed data and verify the system returns the correct validation error messages.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller to get credentials.
Authenticate as a seller.
Provide a product context for the product option.

scenario.draft: Test successful product option creation by an admin for an existing product. After registering and logging in as admin, create a product, then create a new product option under this product, supplying all required business fields. Validate that the option is created and all returned details are correct.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin account, if needed.
Authenticate as admin to get JWT.
Create a product as admin for option linkage.

scenario.draft: Verify error handling when creating a product option with a SKU that already exists for the same product as admin. Create the first option, then attempt to create a second with the identical SKU and expect a uniqueness violation response.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin, as needed.
Authenticate as admin.
Create the product for option creation.
Create the initial option with the target SKU.

scenario.draft: Test that the API properly rejects product option creation requests with missing or invalid input data when initiated by an admin. Expect validation errors for any such failed attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for authentication.
Login as admin to get JWT.
Produce a product for options.

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller can successfully retrieve a paginated and filtered list of product option stock records for an option they own. The flow includes seller registration, login, creating a product, adding a product option, adding several stock records, then retrieving the list of stocks with various filters and pagination parameters. Confirm expected fields and correct data are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register seller account.
Login as seller.
Seller creates a product to get productId.
Create a product option to receive productOptionId.
Create multiple product option stock records for the test option.

scenario.draft: Test the search function when no product option stocks exist or none match the filter criteria. As a seller, attempt to filter by a condition that yields no results and verify the empty result is handled gracefully.

dependencies.purpose: Register seller account.
Seller login.
Set up a product for context.
Product option creation for which no stocks will be created yet.

scenario.draft: Ensure that an admin user can retrieve a paginated, filtered list of stock records for any product option. Register and authenticate as admin, create a product and product option, add multiple stock entries, then search stock records as admin and check the response for correct structure, pagination, and filtering logic.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin account for tests.
Login as admin to get JWT.
Create a product as admin.
Create a product option under the admin's product.
Create multiple stocks for the product option.

scenario.draft: Test that a user without admin privileges (such as a regular customer or unauthenticated caller) cannot retrieve product option stock records as an admin, and receives a permission denied or unauthorized response.

Test updating a product option stock record as an admin. First, ensure a product and associated product option exist. Add a product option stock record to the option. Attempt to update fields such as stock_count and warehouse_location with valid data and verify success. Then check edge cases: try to update the stock to a negative count (should trigger a validation error), attempt an update for a non-existent productOptionStockId (should return not found), try to update an already soft-deleted stock (should fail with an appropriate error), and attempt to update immutable fields if any (should prevent changes and return a validation error). Validate audit log entries for each modification.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product to host the option and its stock modification lifecycle.
Add a product option to the created product in order to create a stock record for testing update scenarios.
Create an initial product option stock record as a prerequisite for update operations.

scenario.draft: Test the soft deletion of a product option stock by the seller. First, set up a seller, create a product owned by that seller, a corresponding product option, and a stock record. Delete the product option stock using its productOptionStockId. Validate that the deleted_at timestamp is set, and the record is no longer returned in active stock searches but remains in the database for auditing. Next, attempt to delete a stock record that has already been soft deleted (should return a suitable error or idempotent response), and attempt to delete a non-existent stockId (should also fail appropriately). Try deleting a stock belonging to a product option not owned by the seller (should result in a permission error).

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller and obtain authentication for subsequent seller-owned actions.
Create a product as the seller for associating a product option.
Create a product option to which the stock is attached.
Create the initial product option stock to set up for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test soft deleting a product option stock by an admin. First, create a product and a product option, and add a product option stock. Soft delete the product option stock and verify that deleted_at is set and the entry is excluded from normal listing. Try to delete the same stock again (expect idempotent or appropriate error response). Test error cases where the stock does not exist or is already deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product and acquire its ID for further operations.
Add a product option to associate the stock with the product.
Create a product option stock record to be deleted during the test.

scenario.draft: Test searching product snapshot history as a seller using filters and pagination. Ensure that the seller owns a product, then create several product snapshots. Search for snapshots using filter criteria (like snapshot_code, snapshot_type, date range). Test that only snapshots for the seller's own product are returned. Attempt to access another seller's product snapshots and verify a permission error. Try using filters that yield no results to validate empty responses. Test access after the product is deleted—ensure that snapshot history for deleted products is still accessible if business logic allows.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account for authenticated context.
Create a product owned by the seller.
Create multiple product snapshots with varied data for rich filtering/search scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test searching product snapshot history as an admin using advanced filters and pagination. After setting up a product with several snapshots, issue snapshot search requests with combinations of snapshot_type, status, snapshot_code, and date range filters. Verify that all snapshots for the product, regardless of ownership, are returned to the admin. Test business edge cases such as requesting with an invalid productId (should return not found/error), and ensure soft-deleted product snapshots are only returned if audit flags are set accordingly. Also, check that attempting to access snapshots for a deleted product returns the correct audit trace or error. Validate correct behavior on pagination and empty result sets.

dependencies.purpose: Create a product as an admin user.
Create multiple snapshots of the product to facilitate comprehensive search and filtering scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a specific product search keyword as a seller. First, register a seller and create a product under their account. Add a search keyword to the product. Retrieve the keyword by its productId and productSearchKeywordId, and verify that all expected details are returned correctly. Ensure the seller has authorization for this operation.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller account for authorization context.
Create a product as the seller to associate a search keyword.
Create a search keyword to use in the retrieval scenario.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a product search keyword with non-existent IDs as a seller. Attempt to get a keyword record using invalid or deleted productId and/or productSearchKeywordId values. Confirm the system returns a 'not found' error and does not leak any internal details. Authorization for the seller must be established before testing this case.

dependencies.purpose: Register and obtain a seller account before attempting keyword retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test admin retrieval of a product's specific search keyword details successfully. Admin must exist and authenticate, then create a product and assign a search keyword. Use the productId and searchKeywordId from previous steps to fetch the details, ensuring that all fields match the created record. Confirm access is permitted to admins, and audit logging is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to perform admin-level operations.
Create a product as admin to associate keywords.
Create a product search keyword for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Try to retrieve a product search keyword as an admin with insufficient or invalid permissions, or as a non-admin user. Confirm that access is properly denied and a permission error is returned. Ensure compliance with RBAC and audit requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for the basic positive path. For negative, attempt without proper admin access or with a revoked role.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create two product search keywords with exactly the same value for the same product as a seller. Expect the first creation to succeed, and the second to fail with a duplicate/validation error indicating uniqueness is enforced. The seller and product must pre-exist for this test.

dependencies.purpose: Seller registration is needed for adding keywords.
Create the target product for the duplicate keyword scenario.
Create the first keyword in order to set up the duplicate context.

scenario.draft: Admin creates a new search keyword for a product successfully. First, register an admin and create a product. Then add a search keyword as admin. Validate the creation response and verify the data via subsequent retrieval. Ensure audit trail recording is enforced as per compliance policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to establish admin context for the scenario.
Create a product using the admin account.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of product search keyword information for a given product as a seller. The seller must register, create a product, add a search keyword, and then update fields such as the keyword value or metadata. Confirm updates are reflected in subsequent GETs and that change history (if applicable) is correctly tracked.

dependencies.purpose: Create seller account for authorization.
Create product as a seller.
Create a product search keyword to be updated.

scenario.draft: Try to update a non-existent product search keyword with invalid productId or keywordId values as a seller. Confirm the system returns a not found error, ensuring no unintended data alterations occur. Ensure authorization is performed before negative testing.

dependencies.purpose: Seller must exist for authorization context.

scenario.draft: Verify that a logged-in customer can search their own product reviews with different filter criteria, such as rating, product, status, AI moderation flags, and keyword search. Include scenarios where filters match multiple reviews, only a single review, and cases where filters match no results. Validate that pagination and ordering parameters return results as expected and do not leak other users' reviews. Ensure error responses are returned for invalid query parameters or when attempting to access reviews outside the customer's own set.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer to access personal review data. Used to obtain a valid JWT session for authorized requests.
Create several product reviews as the test subject to set up the data necessary for searching and filtering scenarios.

scenario.draft: Check that a logged-in seller can search reviews for products they own using various advanced filters (by product, customer, rating range, AI moderation, and date). Validate results only include reviews for that seller's products and that pagination works as intended. Include scenarios for no result cases (no reviews exist for owned products) and edge cases such as large page numbers. Attempt searches where filter values are outside the allowed range and check for error responses. Confirm that sellers cannot see reviews for products they do not own.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an existing seller to access review search features on seller-owned products.
Create or register one or more products for the seller to ensure they have owned products for review association.
Create product reviews on the seller's products by one or more customers to populate data for the search scenarios.

scenario.draft: Confirm that an admin can retrieve a comprehensive, paginated list of all reviews in the system using advanced search and filter criteria (by product, customer, rating, AI moderation status, time window, and keyword). Validate correct enforcement of pagination, ordering, and advanced business rules (e.g., only reviews for existing/active products are returned). Test scenarios where admin applies search filters that restrict results to a narrow subset or return no results. Include edge cases: searches spanning large datasets and invalid or out-of-bounds input for filters. Verify error handling for malformed requests and missing permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin to access global review search capabilities.
Create multiple products as an admin to provide reviewable items for the test. Optionally, ensure some products are soft-deleted or disabled for negative test cases.
Insert product reviews (from one or more customers) for the products to build a dataset for search/filter tests.

scenario.draft: Validate that a customer can fetch the full details of their own review by its unique reviewId, receiving all fields: author, product, order item, rating, status, AI moderation information, timestamps, and text body. Attempt access to a review owned by another customer and confirm a permission denied error is returned. Include a case where the requested reviewId does not exist or references a soft-deleted review to assert correct error handling (not found or appropriate error code).

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as the customer whose review is being fetched.
Create a product review as the test customer so there is a reviewId to fetch for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Check that a seller can retrieve all business-relevant fields of a product review for a product that they own, using the specific reviewId. Confirm that sensitive information and AI moderation context are included as appropriate. Attempt to fetch a review for a product not owned by the seller (should be forbidden), and attempt to fetch a soft-deleted or non-existent review to confirm that correct errors are returned. Validate that valid requests are fully audited and the output matches the schema.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller for permission enforcement.
Create a product for the seller to ensure ownership context exists.
Create a product review as a customer for the seller's product to obtain a valid reviewId for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test a successful update of a seller's own organization profile and business attributes (such as company name, representative name, contact number, and address). Simulate an authenticated seller submitting valid update data. Confirm that all changes are audit logged in the seller_histories table. The response should reflect the updated seller profile, and the system should maintain compliance recordkeeping.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new seller account required to perform profile updates.
Authenticate the seller to obtain credentials/token for authorized update.

scenario.draft: Test update failure when the seller submits invalid or non-compliant data (such as an incorrectly formatted email, missing mandatory fields, or an invalid business number). The response should indicate validation errors as per business rules, and no changes should occur in the profile or histories.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account for update attempt.
Obtain authentication to test update with invalid payload.

scenario.draft: Test the failure scenario where a malicious or unauthenticated actor attempts to update a seller's organization profile without a valid session token or as a different user. The operation should be rejected with an authorization error, no fields should be updated, and audit logs must record the denied attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller as the true owner of the profile.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully update a seller organization's profile for compliance, support, or business operations. The test should cover changes to company name, address, or status, with all modifications logged in the seller_histories table. Create a coupon usage record and capture its couponUsageId for lookup.

Assess error response structure for compliance/audit.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to set up permissions for template creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a compliance event as admin for test setup.

Confirm that related audit logs and compliance records are updated.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to author a review.
Create a new product.
Create an order for eligibility of product review.
Create a product review for later deletion.
Initial delete (soft-delete) of the product review before repeat attempt.

scenario.draft: Validate that deleting a product review with an invalid or non-existent productReviewId returns an error explaining that the record is not found. Confirm that the error response includes meaningful error messages for audit and developer debugging.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate an admin account to test privileged search permissions.
Generate several product inquiries with different customers/products/statuses to provide data for admin-level search coverage.

scenario.draft: Test fetching full detail of a product inquiry as the customer owner. Ensure the returned data includes all fields (customer, product, content, status, AI analysis fields, etc.). Attempt to access a non-existent productInquiryId or one belonging to another customer should return a permission error or 404. The scenario also covers verifying compliance with privacy and field-level access controls for the customer role. Audit logging for inquiry access is also checked.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a customer who will act as inquiry owner.
Create a product inquiry for the customer to be fetched in the detail view test.

scenario.draft: Test successful admin login with valid credentials. Register a new admin using the registration endpoint with a unique email and password, then perform a login using those credentials. Confirm the response includes a valid JWT token in the Authorization header and the admin profile, and all compliance logging is correctly triggered.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account as a prerequisite to obtain credentials for login testing.

scenario.draft: Test failed admin login due to invalid password. Register a new admin, then attempt to log in with the correct email but an incorrect password. Verify that the API returns an error indicating invalid credentials and that no JWT token is provided. Ensure proper audit logging of the failed login attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to have a known valid email for login.

scenario.draft: Test failed admin login with a non-existent email address. Attempt to log in with an email address that does not exist in the system and any password value. Verify the API returns an appropriate error (such as user not found or unauthorized), and ensure that error logging and compliance requirements are met.

Test successful logout of an authenticated admin session. Register and log in as a new admin to obtain a valid JWT, then perform a logout. Confirm that the session is invalidated, subsequent API calls with the same token fail authorization, and audit log entries for logout are created.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to prepare a valid session for logout.
Authenticate as admin to get valid JWT for logout test.

scenario.draft: Test logout attempt without valid authentication. Call the logout endpoint without a valid JWT or with an expired/invalid token. Verify API returns an error indicating there is no active session to log out, and that compliance/audit log reflects the attempt.

Test successful validation of a valid JWT token for admin. Register and log in as an admin to obtain a JWT, then validate the token. Ensure the endpoint confirms authorization status, returns session/profile info, and records audit logs for token validation actions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new admin account for token generation.
Login to obtain a valid JWT token for validation.

scenario.draft: Test failed validation of an invalid or expired admin JWT token. Attempt to validate a clearly invalid or expired JWT token and verify that the API rejects it with proper error messages and auditing.

Test successful change of admin password. Register and log in as a new admin to obtain a valid session. Change the password using the correct current password and a new secure password. Verify the system updates the password, returns a success message, audit logs the change, and invalidates all previous sessions.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account for conducting password changes.
Authenticate as admin to perform password change with valid session.

scenario.draft: Test failure to change password when the current password is incorrect. Register and log in as admin, then attempt a password change, providing an incorrect current password. Confirm the operation fails, password is not changed, a detailed error/code is returned, and an audit entry is created.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account and acquire credentials.
Authenticate to get a valid session for the operation.

scenario.draft: Test successful registration of a new seller account. Provide unique email, valid password, and all required company profile information (company name, business number, representative name, etc.). Confirm that the account is created, JWT tokens are issued in the response headers, onboarding audit and compliance events are logged, and that follow-up login will succeed with these credentials.

Test failure to register a seller when the email already exists. Register a seller with a specific email, then attempt a second registration with the same email. Confirm the API rejects the request with a duplicate email error, does not create a new account, and returns precise error feedback for the user as well as audit/compliance logs.

dependencies.purpose: First registration to establish a duplicate candidate.

scenario.draft: Test failure to register seller with missing required fields. Attempt to register a new seller with missing or invalid (e.g., empty) mandatory fields such as company_name, business_number, or password. Validate that the API returns clear validation errors, does not create the account, and that audit logging captures the failed attempt.

Test failure to register seller with an improperly formatted email address (not RFC compliant or not allowed by business rules). Attempt registration and confirm the API returns an error, does not create an account, and records an audit/compliance event.

Test failure to register seller with an already used business number. Register one seller with a unique business_number, then attempt registration of a new seller using the same business_number with a different email. Confirm the API enforces uniqueness, returns a precise error, and audit logs the attempt.

dependencies.purpose: Register the first seller to create a business_number duplication scenario.

scenario.draft: Test fetching detailed information for a single favorite product using a given favoriteProductId. Cover successful retrieval (for the authenticated customer and if the product is currently favorited), forbidden access (if another user tries to fetch details), and not found scenarios (if the favoriteProductId does not exist or is soft-deleted). Validate the returned fields include favorite and product details. Ensure soft-deleted or non-owned records return an appropriate error indicating either access restriction or missing record.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain a list of currently favorited product IDs for the authenticated customer to use as setup.
Create a favorite product link to ensure a favoriteProductId exists for positive test cases.

scenario.draft: Test adding a product to the authenticated customer's favorite products list using a valid productId. First, verify successful creation when the product is not already favorited, including validation that the link references the correct customer and product. Test duplicate handling by attempting to favorite the same product twice—ensure the system either returns the existing favorite or an error indicating it's already favorited. Also test invalid productId and validation errors (e.g., non-existent or deleted product).

dependencies.purpose: Check for existing favorites to confirm initial state is correct.

scenario.draft: Test updating a favorite product entry's metadata and performing a soft-unfavorite (set deleted_at). Cover successful updates to allowed fields by the authenticated owner, disallowing updates by other users. Ensure proper business logic on soft-unfavorite—after unfavoriting, the record should no longer appear in active queries. Attempt updates on non-existent, non-owned, or already soft-deleted records and verify correct error handling/response codes. Confirm side effects such as notification cleanup or analytics adjustment as appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a favorite product record to provide a valid favoriteProductId for update/unfavorite testing.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting (unfavoriting) a favorite product by its ID for the authenticated customer. Cover the normal path (deleting an existing favorite), and error scenarios, including already soft-deleted entries and unauthorized deletion attempts. Confirm that deleted records do not show in active favorite lists but still exist for audit purposes. Test idempotent behavior on repeat deletion calls and ensure associated notifications or recommendation entries are updated upon unfavoriting. Attempt to delete a favoriteProductId that never existed and verify appropriate error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid favoriteProductId for the test, ensuring the record exists for delete/unfavorite actions.

scenario.draft: Test searching and paginating through a customer's favorite inquiry records. Cover successful retrieval with default and advanced filter criteria (e.g. by inquiry status, title/content, date ranges) and proper pagination. Validate that only favorites belonging to the authenticated customer are returned, and that soft-deleted (unfavorited) entries and inaccessible records are excluded. Test edge cases of empty result sets, invalid filters, unauthorized access attempts, and out-of-bounds pagination parameters. Ensure auditing and notification requirements are respected as described in the business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Establish at least one favorite inquiry record for the user to enable search/filter testing.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a specific order item detail by the owning customer. First, create a new customer and log in to receive an authentication token. Next, create an order for this customer, add an order item, and then fetch the detail of that specific order item using its orderId and orderItemId. Validate that the returned item information matches expected fields and that access is granted. This test simulates a typical user reviewing their order item after purchase.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer account to obtain user identity and permission context.
Authenticate as the newly registered customer to obtain a JWT token for authorized API access.
Create a new order for the customer so there is an order context to add items to.
Add a new item to the created order and obtain the orderItemId needed for the GET detail test.

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated customer cannot access the order item detail of another customer's order. Register two distinct customer accounts. Have the first customer place an order and add an order item. Attempt to fetch the order item detail as the second customer using the same orderId and orderItemId, and confirm that the system returns a 'forbidden' error response to enforce ownership access control.

dependencies.purpose: Register both customers needed for this test, ensuring separate identities.
Log into each customer account as part of the test sequence.
Create an order for the first customer to own the test order item.
Add an item to the order, establishing the context for secure ownership.

scenario.draft: Test handling of requests for a non-existent order item. Register and authenticate a customer, create an order, and attempt to fetch an order item detail using an invalid or random orderItemId that does not exist under the specified orderId. Verify that the system returns an appropriate 'not found' error, validating error handling for invalid references.

dependencies.purpose: Register customer for authentication context.
Authenticate as the customer.
Create an order to provide a legitimate orderId for testing error response to non-existent orderItemId.

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated seller can view the details of an order item associated with their product sale. Register a seller account, create a product, and make a sale via a customer order. The seller then retrieves the order item detail using the correct orderId and orderItemId. The test validates proper business linkage, access permissions, and that the returned data is correct for the seller's product.

dependencies.purpose: Register a seller to manage products and monitor order sales.
Authenticate as the seller for JWT authorization.
Create a product under the seller's ownership to be included in customer orders.
Register a customer to simulate a buyer.
Login as customer to place an order.
Customer creates an order for the seller's product.
Customer adds an order item referencing the seller's product, enabling the seller to later check details.

scenario.draft: Test that a seller cannot access the details of an order item not related to their own product sales. Register two sellers, ensure a product and order for the first seller, then attempt to fetch the order item detail as the second seller. Validate the system returns a 'forbidden' or similar access-denied response, ensuring robust enforcement of data privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Create both seller accounts to establish separate business entities.
Login as the second seller to attempt unauthorized data access.
Register a product owned by Seller 1 for sale.
Register a customer for test ordering.
Customer login for order placement.
Customer order referencing Seller 1's product.
Customer creates an order item for Seller 1's product.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin user can retrieve details of any order item across the system, regardless of order ownership. Register an admin user, create a customer and order with an order item, then have the admin fetch the order item detail. Verify all fields are viewable and compliance/audit access is logged as per policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user for privileged access.
Authenticate as admin for JWT token.
Register a customer to create an order with items.
Login as customer to initiate order.
Create order for the customer.
Create order item under the customer's order, setup for admin testing.

scenario.draft: Verify that the system returns an appropriate error when an admin tries to fetch an order item detail using an invalid or non-existent orderItemId. Register an admin, and attempt to fetch with a fake or random ID. The response should be a 'not found' error, confirming correct error handling for invalid identifiers at admin level.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin to perform the test with high privileges.
Authenticate as admin.

scenario.draft: Test the ability for an authenticated customer to add a new item to one of their orders. Register and login a customer, create a new order, then post a new order item referencing a valid product. Validate the response includes the created item, proper snapshot linkage, and order item constraints are enforced (e.g., quantity, valid product relationship).

dependencies.purpose: Register new customer.
Authenticate for API access.
Create seller for the product catalog.
Seller login to create products.
Seller creates a new product to be ordered.
Customer creates a new order in which the order item will be added.

scenario.draft: Verify that the system returns an error when attempting to add an order item referencing a productId that does not exist or is not available. Register and login as customer, create a new order, then attempt to add an order item with a random or non-existent productId. Confirm system rejects the creation with a validation or not found error response.

dependencies.purpose: Register customer.
Login as customer for authorized operation.
Create order for context in which to add the item.

scenario.draft: Attempt to add an order item to an order while unauthenticated (no JWT token provided). Confirm that the system denies the operation, returning an 'unauthorized' or 'authentication required' error. This tests enforcement of access controls on item creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create an order context (if required) to which to attempt the unauthorized add action.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can directly add a new order item to any customer's order. Register an admin, register a customer and create an order for them, then have the admin add a new order item to this order. Validate the admin's ability to create items across ownership boundaries, and that the created item is associated with the correct order.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for privileged action.
Login as admin to obtain necessary JWT.
Create a customer to own the target order.
Customer logs in to create the order.
Create the target order for admin's order item insertion.

scenario.draft: Verify that the admin receives an error when trying to add an order item referencing a non-existent or invalid product. Register admin, create a customer and an order, then attempt to add an order item referencing a fake productId. The response should be a validation error or 'not found' error, validating input constraint enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin.
Authenticate as admin.
Create customer for the order context.
Customer logs in to create the order.
Create an order to which admin will attempt to attach an invalid order item.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of coupon snapshots with advanced filtering and pagination as an admin. Simulate different filter, sort, and pagination parameters (e.g., by couponTemplateId, created_at range, status), ensuring that only admin-role accounts have access and the returned data matches the filters. Edge cases include empty results and large result sets. Also, verify error handling for malformed queries and unauthorized access. Use dependency to authenticate as admin user before the request.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.

scenario.draft: Test fetching a specific coupon snapshot detail by its UUID as admin. Scenario 1: Successful retrieval for an existing, non-deleted snapshot. Scenario 2: Attempt to fetch a non-existent or soft-deleted snapshot, verifying correct not-found/appropriate error is returned. Check that only admin-role accounts can access the detail. Dependency: Authenticate as admin before executing the GET request.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new coupon snapshot as an admin. Scenario 1: Provide valid payload with correct references to an existing coupon and event context, expect successful creation with compliance audit fields. Scenario 2: Attempt to create a snapshot with duplicate (already used) data or invalid reference (e.g., non-existent issued coupon or event), ensuring system returns validation or conflict error. Edge: Missing required field. Dependency: Authenticate as admin and create a valid issued coupon before snapshot creation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.
Issue a valid coupon to be referenced in the snapshot payload.

scenario.draft: Update allowed fields of a coupon snapshot record as an admin. Scenario: Update metadata or permissible fields (not evidence/immutable data) for an existing, non-deleted snapshot and verify success. Try forbidden mutations (changing immutable fields or for a non-existent/deleted snapshot) and verify validation or error responses. Ensure audit logging occurs as required. Dependency: Create a valid coupon snapshot before updating.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.
Create a coupon snapshot that will be targeted for updates.

scenario.draft: Perform soft-delete of a coupon snapshot by its UUID as admin. Scenario 1: Delete an existing, active coupon snapshot and verify 'deleted_at' is set and record is omitted from active listings, but still retained for audit. Scenario 2: Attempt to delete a non-existent or already-deleted snapshot and verify not-found or idempotency is correctly handled. Confirm only admin role can delete, and that audit/compliance traces are logged. Dependency: Create and optionally delete a coupon snapshot.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain JWT for authorization.
Create a coupon snapshot for testing deletion.

scenario.draft: Test searching favorite snapshot records as an admin using advanced filtering options. Cover scenarios including search by time window, object type (product, inquiry, address), customer constraints, and keyword queries on snapshot contents. Validate correct pagination, sorting, and access control. Confirm that only authorized admin users can retrieve snapshot details. Verify correct behavior for empty searches, invalid filter parameters, and permission errors. Edge cases should include requests with no matching data and searches at page boundaries.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to acquire a valid admin JWT for testing authorized access.
Login as an admin to obtain JWT for authorization when listing favorite snapshots.

scenario.draft: Test fetching a favorite snapshot record by its unique ID as the owner (customer). Validate that only the owner or authorized admin can access the record. Ensure the response contains historical snapshot content as expected, and that attempts to access non-existent, deleted, or non-owned snapshots yield suitable errors. Edge cases should include requesting with unauthorized users and soft-deleted records.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account to serve as the owner of the favorite snapshot.
Login as the customer to obtain JWT for authorized requests.
Favorite a product as the customer, creating a favorite record needed to snapshot.
Create a favorite snapshot for the customer to retrieve by ID.

scenario.draft: Test fetching a favorite snapshot record by its unique ID as an admin, who is not the owner. Validate proper permission checks and information disclosure consistent with admin roles. Cover attempts to retrieve existing, deleted, and non-existent snapshot records, ensuring correct error codes and audit trail enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer to create a favorite and related snapshot.
Allow creation of favorite product and favorite snapshot as a customer.
Create a favorite product as the customer for snapshot creation.
Customer creates a favorite snapshot to be accessed by admin.
Register a new admin for snapshot retrieval.
Login as admin to obtain token for authorized get requests.

scenario.draft: Test creating a favorite snapshot for a valid, active favorite object (e.g., product, inquiry, or address) as the owner customer. Validate that the snapshot record is correctly created and returned, including all references and serialized object state. Then, attempt to create a duplicate snapshot for the same favorite object and verify that the system properly enforces idempotency or returns an appropriate error, per business logic. Also test creating a snapshot for a favorite object that is not active (e.g., soft-deleted) or not owned by the customer, confirming correct business rule enforcement and error messages.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer account as the owner of the favorite.
Login as customer to perform authed operations.
Create a favorite object (product) as a prerequisite for snapshot creation.

scenario.draft: Test updating a favorite snapshot record as the snapshot's owner, modifying permitted metadata or object state. Validate that only allowed fields are updateable—attempts to change immutable or restricted fields (such as creation timestamp) must be rejected. Test error handling for updating non-existent, deleted, or non-owned favoriteSnapshotId records. Confirm successful updates are reflected in the returned entity, and non-permitted fields remain unchanged. Ensure security checks for role and ownership are strictly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as a customer to act as snapshot owner.
Obtain authentication for performing snapshot creation and update.
Create a favorite product as a base for the snapshot.
Create an initial favorite snapshot as the customer, for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test updating mutable metadata for an existing product review snapshot by an admin. First, create a customer and log in, then have the customer create a product, place an order, and write a product review. Have the customer (or admin) create a snapshot of the review. Finally, as an admin, update the metadata for a review snapshot (such as compliance annotations or context) and verify the update is reflected, previous audit trail is preserved, and no illegal fields (core review content, timestamps) can be changed. Verify success and audit integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate an admin user to perform the update.
Create a customer account for review creation.
Authenticate the customer for subsequent operations.
Create a product review to ensure a valid review context for snapshot creation.
Create a review snapshot for the product review to allow later update.

scenario.draft: Test update failure when trying to modify immutable fields (e.g., core review content, rating, created_at) of an existing review snapshot by an admin. Attempt to change a protected field and verify that the API rejects the request, returns a descriptive error, does not alter snapshot data or audit trail, and enforces compliance policies.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate an admin user account.
Create a customer for the review creation.
Authenticate as the customer.
Create a product review to establish review context.
Create a review snapshot to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test soft deletion (erase) of a product review snapshot by an admin. Create a customer and their product review, have the admin create a snapshot for the review, then, as admin, delete the snapshot (soft delete). Verify that the snapshot is excluded from standard queries, audit log records the action, and other snapshots remain accessible. Confirm that deletion is not permitted if the snapshot is under a compliance lock or legal hold.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account and log in.
Register a customer to create product reviews.
Authenticate as customer.
Create a product review for snapshotting.
Create a review snapshot for testing deletion.

scenario.draft: Test idempotency and error handling for repeated or invalid review snapshot soft deletion. After deleting a review snapshot, attempt to delete it again and confirm the API returns an appropriate error or idempotent success. Also, attempt to delete a non-existent snapshot and validate the error response is precise and audit-tracked.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare an admin user for erase action.
Create a customer for context.
Customer login for review creation.
Produce a review and snapshot to delete.
Create the target review snapshot.

scenario.draft: Test advanced search and filtering of moderation events by an admin. Insert multiple moderation events (covering different event types, actors, review/inquiry targets, and date ranges) and query them with different filter criteria (by event type, actor_type, date, or specific target entities). Validate that only the correct, authorized, and relevant moderation events are returned, responses are paginated, and sensitive data is filtered or exposed as per admin role. Edge cases: search with empty filter returns all (up to page limit), filters for non-existent criteria return empty result, and pagination works correctly.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for advanced search access.
Insert moderation event records with diverse values for search testing.

scenario.draft: Test search request as a non-admin (e.g., customer or seller) and confirm the API returns an authorization error and logs the access attempt for compliance. Create a non-admin user, authenticate, then attempt to search moderation events as this user.

dependencies.purpose: Register a customer for unauthorized access.
Authenticate as the customer.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of moderation event detail by UUID as an admin. First, create an admin, then insert a moderation event. Call the GET endpoint with the correct moderationEventId and validate the complete event data (event type, actor, target entities, reasons, evidence, timestamp) is accurate, sensitive fields are included, and audit logs record the access.

dependencies.purpose: Create and login as an admin to get moderation event details.
Insert a moderation event to query by ID.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when retrieving a moderationEventId that does not exist or has been deleted. As an admin, attempt to fetch a detail with a random or erased UUID, verify a not-found error is returned, and confirm audit logs are updated for compliance and incident traceability.

dependencies.purpose: Admin context for the GET request.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new moderation event by an admin for a review or inquiry. Steps: prepare a resource (e.g., a product review or inquiry), have an admin trigger a POST with event details such as type, actor, target entity, evidence references, and reason. Validate that the moderation event is persisted, all business-required fields are present, the target status is updated accordingly (e.g., review blocked/unblocked), and the event is recorded in audit/compliance logs. Subsequent GET/listing should include this moderation event.

dependencies.purpose: Admin account creation to perform moderation action.
Create a product review to moderate (alternatively, use a product inquiry as target).

scenario.draft: Test failure case for creation of moderation event with invalid parameters (e.g., missing required field, referencing non-existent review/inquiry, or providing illegal event_type). Ensure API validation triggers, returns explicit error messages, does not create the moderation event, and audits the failed attempt for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Admin user for context.

Ensure that the response returns a correctly filtered, sorted, and paginated set of results. Validate that only users with admin role can access full results, and that empty searches result in empty datasets with valid pagination. Attempt with both matching and non-matching filters to cover happy path and no-result scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin to receive a valid JWT token required to authorize the order group search.
Create at least one order group as test data before attempting to search and filter.

scenario.draft: Test that a non-admin user (customer or seller) is denied access when attempting to search admin order groups. Attempt the API with an invalid or missing JWT token, expecting a forbidden error or invalid authentication response. Validate security and RBAC configuration.

Test failure when the admin tries to search for order groups using invalid search or filter parameters (e.g., invalid sort parameter, malformed filter conditions). The system should return a meaningful error (e.g., validation failed) and compliance-appropriate error code. Confirm no data is leaked and the error structure is useful for troubleshooting.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for permission to access the endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of an order group by its ID for a customer who is authorized to view the group. Ensure all relevant order group details (metadata, notes, and batch references) are included. Also test that another customer who does not own the group cannot access the order group, and receives an appropriate permission denied error. Cover edge cases such as invalid UUID format and group not found.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to simulate a user-facing scenario.
Obtain a JWT token for customer who owns the order group.
Create an order group and assign it to the test customer.

scenario.draft: Test successful detailed retrieval of an order group by group ID for an authorized seller. Validate that all business metadata is accurate and complete. Attempt to retrieve a group with a seller who does not have ownership or permission and confirm a forbidden or not-found error is returned. Also test error cases for missing or malformed orderGroupId parameter.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller to simulate selling context.

scenario.draft: Validate admin can successfully retrieve complete details for an order group by its ID, seeing all admin-only fields. Cover edge cases such as requesting with a nonexistent orderGroupId (should return not found), attempting with an invalid UUID format, or with insufficient permissions/non-admin context (should return forbidden or error). Confirm audit is triggered for such access.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin for permission.

scenario.draft: Verify admin is able to successfully create a new order group by supplying all required fields. Validate system response structure and side effects such as audit event creation. Also test failures for missing, malformed, or unauthorized parameters.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to enable order group creation.

Confirm that returned data matches the record in the underlying audit table, and no sensitive data is disclosed beyond permitted scope.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate admin and obtain JWT for authorization.
Search and retrieve a list of existing access logs to extract a valid accessLogId for detail retrieval.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate admin and obtain JWT for authorization.

scenario.draft: Test unauthorized access to a specific access log. Attempt the request as a non-admin user (e.g., as a customer or seller), or with no token, or with a revoked JWT. dependencies.purpose: Register a customer to acquire a non-admin JWT for negative test.
